children: ICICI Securities research report on Prime Focus

Post-COVID, global audiences have become more demanding with regard to the experiential aspect of what they watch in theatres. The proportion of visual effects in movie budgets has increased from 5-20% to 20-40% in tentpole productions (in India and globally). We think this is structural, and Prime Focus is likely to be a key beneficiary. DNEG has won 8 Oscars in the last 15 years (3 in the last 5) and is a key partner for the largest global production houses. Additionally, Brahma AI, which has proprietary models such as ATMAN (photorealistic digital human) and VAANI (voice and visual localisation engine), is helping it diversify its client base beyond the M&E industry and has material optionality. Also, if the recently announced fund raise (link) helps to reduce their debt burden, there is room for further re-rating.
We initiate with a BUY rating and a TP of INR 375 using our 3-stage DCF model (implied EV/EBITDA of 17.5x FY28E).
